newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel, jet down on crude fall.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel, jet down on crude fall.

text.p: Singapore gas oil and jet fuel markets were pressured by the slide in crude and gas oil futures prices on London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE), traders said.

Brent crude fell below the $20.00 mark to last trade at $19.89 a barrel, while gas oil futures lost $3.50 a tonne to last trade at $170.25 causing Singapore swaps gas oil to dip below the $25.50 support.
Gas oil swaps were also under sustained selling pressure with March last quoted at $25.20/$25.30 a barrel, as several traders position themselves to bring in cargoes from the west.
The East-West spread is now seen close to $19 a tonne, which was making it increasingly attractive to bring in European cargoes, traders said.

Traders said while China was not in a hurry to buy for March, a US major which was planning a one-month shutdown from March 15 at its Singapore refinery, would soon need to buy more gas oil cargoes to store in their terminal in Hong Kong.

The major recently bought a cargo for early March at $1.10 a barrel over Singapore spot quotes, cost-and-freight Hong Kong. The market was also focussed on India's tender for April. The market consensus was that India might take 700,000 tonnes, in line with their purchase of 720,000 tonnes in April 1996. But some traders said India might take more than that which would help support prices.

Offers into the tender were aggressive with west coast cargoes seen between $1.40 and $1.96 a barrel above MidEast quotes, c-and-f, compared with around $2.22 premium for March. East coast offers were seen between $2.00 and $2.80 a barrel above MidEast quotes, compared with around $3.00 premiums in March.
Physical gas oil was offered on Friday at $25.15 a barrel for mid-March lifting fob, with a bid seen at $25.00, down from the deal on Thursday at $25.45.

Jet fuel also slipped below $28.00, pressured by dormant regional demand so far as the market awaited Indonesia's demand for March and April when the Hajj pilgrimage season starts. An offer was seen at $27.80 for March 16-20 lifting fob, with buyers at bay.
Swaps kerosene for March was traded at a low $27.00 a barrel with the jet fuel/gas oil regrade plunging to $1.60/$1.85 a barrel, down from the $2.50/$2.80 range seen for most of the week.
